(4) The two programs, redevelopment and rehabilitation, will provide a total approach at the physical problems of the Randolph Community. Home improvement loans and grants will be available in addition to relocation payments and homeownership opportunities. Community facilities will be built and those existing improved. In total, the Randolph Community should offer more opportunity and better living conditions than could be found in other areas of Richmond for the same socioeconomic level.
(5) Housing projects are planned in two locations for the elderly. As a planned goal of the Community, the residents are very much in favor of elderly housing and through their PAC group have established these projects as an early community priority.
It can be expected that some of the residents will relocate out of the Randolph area. Many will relocate probably due to the construction inconveniences and a variety of other personal reasons. Analyses of the housing market in the Richmond Metropolitan Area would indicate the largest number of new homes and apartments are being built in the surrounding counties. It is unlikely that many Randolph citizens will be attracted to these areas. Conversely, it can be expected that because of its location adjacent to the Virginia Commonwealth University and the central city more integration will be likely when apartments are available to individuals outside of the community. It should be further noted that the Randolph Community is adjacent to the "Fan" area of the city, an area very popular to students, professionals, and young homeowners. This is not to imply that the Randolph Community has the same "old city" charm as the Fan area, but it does imply that Randolph could experience a "spillover" if new apartment units are available.
With consideration of all the factors mentioned the socioeconomic character of the Randolph Community is expected to experience little change due to the proposed projects impact.
3. Dislocation and Relocation:
a. Families and Individuals to be Relocated:
During the first 20 months of the project 166 families will be relocated. Over an estimated eight year period a total of 1,814 families and individuals will have to be relocated.
